name: Red-Violet (Crayola)
lede: Red-Violet (Crayola) is a Crayola crayon shade whose name states its own mixture: a violet pulled toward red.

sections.title: A plain compound name
sections.body:
Crayola often names a crayon by stating the two hues it sits between rather than inventing a word, and this is one of those names [1]. The color library records it from a Wikipedia-sourced list of Crayola crayon colors; no book consulted here gives an exact release date for this particular label, so that date is undocumented [1]. The hex value #C0448F is a screen approximation of a printed crayon wrapper, not a measured pigment [1].

Its nearest neighbor in the library is [[mulberry]], about 2.6 units away in LCH space, close enough that the two look almost the same on an uncalibrated screen [1]. [[red-violet]] is the plainer form of the same compound name, used in other systems without the Crayola brand attached to it [1].

Other close matches in the library include [[mulberry-crayola]] and the more vivid [[fandango]], both within a few LCH units of this swatch [1].

sections.title: Field notes
sections.body: In the ColorHub painting archive this hue is close to unique, matching only 1 of 23,781 paintings, as photographed [2]. That single match is a painting from India dated 1900, and the color turns up far more often in Indian works than the archive average, though a sample of one says more about the hue's rarity than about any real pattern [2].
